claims.text: Oxygen uptake in Group IV-containing refractory high-entropy alloys promotes brittle alpha-HCP precipitation and catastrophic cracking.
A dwell at 400-500°C for 1-2 hours is sufficient to completely decompose the refractory-metal hydride precursors.
Maintaining a vacuum below 10^-5 torr during initial heating permits complete hydrogen evolution without oxide formation.
An oxygen concentration below 1 ppm in the inert processing atmosphere is required to avoid harmful oxygen uptake.
Rapid heating to approximately 0.7-0.8 Tm, identified as 1100-1200°C for the proposed alloys, suppresses grain growth and alpha-HCP nucleation.
Oxygen uptake is most aggressive in the 600-900°C temperature range.
Alloying Mo- or W-based BCC refractory alloys with Group IV elements can alter electronic structure and promote an intrinsic brittle-to-ductile transition.
Electronic-structure modifications induced by Group IV elements stabilize a single BCC solid solution in the proposed RHEA.
Rapid thermal cycling and extrusion produce a refined grain size below 10 micrometers.
Grain refinement enhances high-temperature yield strength by impeding dislocation motion.
The proposed process will produce a bulk alloy exceeding 98% of theoretical density.
The processed alloy will have room-temperature yield strength above 800 MPa.
The processed alloy will retain yield strength above 400 MPa at 1000°C.
The processed alloy will sustain more than 5% compressive strain at room temperature.
The processed alloy will contain a negligible alpha-HCP phase fraction.
Conventional powder-metallurgy processing without controlled hydride decomposition typically raises oxygen content above 500 ppm.
Uncontrolled conventional processing produces alpha-HCP precipitation and brittle fracture during extrusion.
The BCC solubility limit for Group IV elements in the proposed alloys is typically below 15 at.%.
The starting powder mixture has an initial oxygen content below 100 ppm.
Changing the Group IV element among Ti, Zr, and Hf may change the predicted yield strength by approximately plus or minus 50 MPa.

contradictions.description: The intervention specifies extrusion under a vacuum below 10^-5 torr, whereas the hypothesis and conditions also permit extrusion under inert argon. It is therefore unclear whether high vacuum during extrusion is mandatory or optional.
